resource_location_routing: getResource first asserts location is non-null. It asks registered ProtocolResolvers in iteration order with (location, this), returning the first non-null Resource before any built-in route; a null result allows the next resolver or built-in logic. Registration uses the loader's LinkedHashSet, preserving its normal registration order.

A leading slash uses getResourceByPath. Otherwise classpath: strips that prefix and constructs ClassPathResource with getClassLoader; classpath*: strips its own prefix and constructs ClassPathAllResource. The default getResourceByPath constructs ClassPathContextResource with the supplied path and loader; a leading slash is not by itself a filesystem-resource route.

Remaining locations are passed to ResourceUtils.toURL, then ResourceUtils.isFileURL selects FileUrlResource versus UrlResource. The classifier recognizes file, vfsfile and vfs protocols. A MalformedURLException causes fallback to getResourceByPath; the catch is not a blanket catch for all resolver/setup exceptions.

This routing creates/returns resource handles, not proof of resource existence and not a stream open. A custom resolver may override standard rules; the question's unmodified default path hook is classpath-based, not evidence that every ResourceLoader subclass behaves that way.
classpath_coordinates: The ClassLoader constructor asserts a non-null path, applies StringUtils.cleanPath, removes one leading slash from that cleaned result, and stores it as both path and absolutePath. It stores the supplied loader or ClassUtils.getDefaultClassLoader and clears clazz; the one-argument constructor delegates to this form with a null loader.

The Class constructor also validates/cleans path but retains that cleaned path for Class-based lookup. Its absolutePath prepends the class's package resource path when clazz is non-null and the path has no leading slash, or removes a leading slash for an absolute path. It stores clazz and sets the classLoader field to null; with a null clazz it falls through to system lookup later rather than explicitly storing a newly selected default loader.

getPath returns absolutePath, which need not equal the stored class-relative path. getClassLoader exposes clazz.getClassLoader when a Class is present, otherwise the stored loader. DefaultResourceLoader.getClassLoader selects its explicit loader or ClassUtils.getDefaultClassLoader before constructing a handle; the constructed handle's stored context is not re-selected from the thread context on every read.

cleanPath performs lexical cleaning such as dot/parent-segment suppression and slash normalization. This is not a filesystem containment or path-traversal defense; normalization alone establishes neither existence nor secure access. No enumeration of the complete StringUtils algorithm is required.
classpath_url_lookup: resolveURL uses clazz.getResource(path) when clazz is present, otherwise classLoader.getResource(absolutePath) when a loader is present, otherwise ClassLoader.getSystemResource(absolutePath). The class-relative path must not be substituted with absolutePath in the Class branch.

resolveURL catches IllegalArgumentException and returns null; it does not catch every possible failure. exists simply tests whether resolveURL returns non-null, while getURL calls it and throws FileNotFoundException on null or returns the URL otherwise.

URL resolution/exists does not open or retain an InputStream and cannot guarantee a later independent stream lookup will succeed. Missing URL lookup is a false result for exists but an exception for getURL, not a uniformly nullable public result.
classpath_stream_access: getInputStream directly calls clazz.getResourceAsStream(path), classLoader.getResourceAsStream(absolutePath), or ClassLoader.getSystemResourceAsStream(absolutePath), in that priority order according to the stored context. It does not obtain a URL from resolveURL and then open that URL.

A null returned stream causes FileNotFoundException using the resource description; a non-null stream is returned to the caller. This method does not include resolveURL's IllegalArgumentException catch, so that URL-helper suppression must not be attributed to stream lookup.

The successful stream is not closed by getInputStream itself, and this method has no stream/content cache. Each invocation performs its own selected lookup; returning a handle earlier or observing exists is not a successful-read guarantee.
classpath_relative_handles: Ordinary ClassPathResource.createRelative passes its stored path, not necessarily getPath/absolutePath, and relativePath to StringUtils.applyRelativePath, then constructs a new ClassPathResource preserving clazz when present or otherwise the stored classLoader.

applyRelativePath finds the last slash and keeps the base up to that slash, replacing its final segment with the relative argument. It inserts a slash only when the relative argument does not start with one; a leading slash in the relative argument does not automatically discard a nonempty base directory. With no slash in the base it returns relativePath directly.

The new constructor cleans the combined path again and retains the appropriate lookup context. Relative construction is lexical and does not check existence, open content or establish filesystem containment.

The default loader's ClassPathContextResource implements ContextResource: getPathWithinContext returns getPath. Its override applies the helper to getPath and constructs another ClassPathContextResource with getClassLoader, preserving the context subtype rather than returning only a plain ClassPathResource.
